_about: Chassis. Not classes: any silhouette, any component in any slot. Numbers are in tens. hardpoints is the die size. loadout is the default components; if their faces total fewer than hardpoints, filler fills the rest. passive is zero or one object: name and description are shown (the codex prints NAME: description), effects are what the engine runs, at most three, one idea (an upside and its cost count as one passive); the validator refuses effects the engine cannot execute. Shown to the player: codex (the inspect entry, combat and hangar), flavour (an in-world quote), the passive's name and description. design is internal and never shown: fantasy (pitch, inspiration, homages), niche (the role it is meant to fill). Makers are placeholders.

makers.name: Halvard Heavy Works
makers.style: Armour first. Everything is a tank, even the ones with legs.
makers.voice: Maintenance manual. Terse, exact, proud of tolerances.

makers.name: Kestrel Dynamics
makers.style: Fast, fragile, over-tuned. Airframes and interceptors.

makers.name: Orrin & Pike
makers.style: Quads and artillery. Old firm, odd designs, everything works.

entries.name: Bulwark

design.fantasy: A repurposed mining vehicle, designed to take severe punishment and keep on tracking. Refurbishments were minimal, basically bolting on weapons and armour, it keeps most of its utilitarian mining machinery flavour.

entries.codex: The Halvard EX-45L (colloquially nicknamed the "Badger") was a mining mech widely praised for its reliability and durability, being designed to operate in the harshest, deepest environments imaginable. Reports exist of Badgers being caught in cave-ins at 5 kilometers underground, only to dig their way out to the surface a day later, just in time for drinks with the crew. So naturally, when the Rifts opened, the ever-practical Halvard engineering team's first instinct was to finally give their prized Badger claws, teeth, and as many missiles as it could carry, putting its legendary longevity to work on the battlefield.

passive.name: Reinforced Skeleton
passive.description: Halvard does not build guns that whiff.

entries.flavour: Hey Russ, ain't that yer Badger over there, covered in demon innards? I thought they retired the ol' girl!

entries.name: Sentinel

design.fantasy: Four legs, six hardpoints, no strong opinions. The one you build around.

entries.codex: The Orrin & Pike general-purpose walker. Six hardpoints and no opinions about what goes in them; whatever the squad is missing, this is where it gets bolted on.
entries.flavour: Orrin & Pike walker frame. Six hardpoints, no favourites. The one that comes back.

entries.name: Raptor

design.fantasy: A priority-target assassin. Hit, run, and let someone else carry the fire extinguisher.

entries.codex: Kestrel's interceptor. Hits twice as hard as anything its size and runs twice as hot doing it. Somebody else carries the fire extinguisher.

passive.name: Hot Hands
passive.description: Everything it fires, it fires too hard.

entries.flavour: Kestrel interceptor airframe. Reactor governor removed by field order. Run it hot and trust the housing.

entries.name: Anvil

design.fantasy: Sits at the back of the fight and ruins the back of theirs.

entries.codex: Orrin & Pike's fire-support walker. Reaches their back rank from ours, and what it sets alight stays alight.

passive.name: Hot Load
passive.description: When an Orrin & Pike shell lands right, it keeps burning.

entries.flavour: Orrin & Pike fire-support walker. Sits behind the line and unmakes the far side of the fight.
